# Zorkian Stories 1: G.U.E.

Local Blorb matches fresh archive container bytes. Its indexed ZCOD payload is Z8 R1/121014 and embedded iFiction metadata independently agrees on title, author and release. The full start-to-finish Matt Goh solution supplies no release/serial; guide edition remains unspecified. A released complete first story, not a port of another registered Zork title.

Follow the mansion/underground route through the wizard and demon confrontation and the final search, requiring the actual authored victory/concluding narrative. The guide describes a completed 21-of-25 route; preserve that legitimate ending without turning 25 points into a completion requirement. Combat death, intermediate passages, score alone and the word victory in the guide are insufficient.

Combat outcomes can vary; checkpoint safely before hazards and use observed state rather than blindly repeating the guide's G commands. The guide has the apparent typo "throw skull in put"; preserve its raw text and adapt only from actual room/parser evidence. Menu confirmation Y belongs only to the displayed question. The clear G.U.E./Zork setting is conservatively grouped with existing zork-i development games.

CENTRAL architecture: story files, full guides, provenance and interpreter execution remain on the central host. Pis receive only small broker help excerpts, never story files or full guides. Do not stage or copy these assets to a Pi. Do not expose central guide/source paths or URLs to Muse. Use small topic-specific broker help excerpts only (at most 9 lines / 1000 characters); no full-guide reads, direct URL access or serial excerpts to reconstruct the guide. Hints are suggested help, not observed success. Resolve startup questions/key pauses first. Make an early safe checkpoint and milestone saves only at confirmed ordinary command prompts; verify actual success. Menu Enter means an empty command, not literal space or the word RETURN; other keys only as requested on screen. On timeout use await_output only: no flush commands, extra keys, repeated input or new SAVE. Collect useful varied labeled synthetic probes and actual same-intent repairs with event IDs, not quotas or repeated filler. Use one command at a time near hazards/questions/menus. Parent independently verifies actual concluding narrative against raw output. No training, evaluation or publication.
content.checkpoint_policy: Early safe checkpoint and milestone saves via the central broker only, at confirmed ordinary command prompts; verify actual success. Resolve questions/key pauses first. Never save to flush a timeout.

# Progress — zorkian-stories-1-gue

Location: Intersection (ancient gate blocks east; tunnels N/W/S). Came via Secret Passage -> Long Tunnel -> Intersection.
Inventory (observed e00006): elvish sword, small lantern (providing light), backpack (worn, open, empty).
Score: +1 after pushing eyes (e00010).

Route: Vault -> push eyes -> open wall (=open fresco) -> enter fresco -> Secret Passage -> north to Ancient Shrine (altar empty, bones refuse take) -> south back -> east to Long Tunnel -> east to Intersection.

Cases:
- vault-eyes-touch: e00009 touch eye accepted (none) annotated e00014
- vault-fresco-open: e00011 open wall accepted (none) annotated e00015
- shrine-bones-take: e00021 take bones refused "You'd rather not" (pending annotation decision; correct refusal, no repair)

Checkpoints: start-vault; secret-passage (verified e00016/e00017).
Last hint: none.
Next: examine gate at Intersection; probe blocked east; explore N/S; checkpoint before hazards.

content.response:
Finally making it to the Eastlands, you find a shaft leading to the depths of 
the Great Underground Empire where, supposedly, lost treasures that have been 
forgotten for centuries are waiting to be found again.

Zorkian Stories 1: G.U.E.
A diversion by Marshal Tenner Winter
Release 1 / Serial number 121014 / Inform 7 build 6G60 (I6/v6.32 lib 6/12N) SD

Vault
This chamber is made of black stone.  The walls are pocked with age; showing 
faded frescos, the subject of which can no longer be determined.  The only exit 
is west, into a long. sloping tunnel that eventually leads back outside.  The 
weight of stone presses upon you, and you feel you must be deep underground.

>

events.intent: Describe current surroundings at game start
events.response:
Vault
This chamber is made of black stone.  The walls are pocked with age; showing 
faded frescos, the subject of which can no longer be determined.  The only exit 
is west, into a long. sloping tunnel that eventually leads back outside.  The 
weight of stone presses upon you, and you feel you must be deep underground.

>
Save to file:

Saved to '/work/experiments/lanthorn-recall-training/play/zorkian-stories-1-gue/saves/ZorkianStories1-GUE.zblorb.save/start-vault.sav.qzl'.
Ok.

>

events.intent: Exit the Vault westward
events.response:
You feel that to leave now would make this entire expedition a waste, so you 
decide not to travel back up the tunnel to the surface.

>

events.intent: Check starting inventory
events.response:
You are carrying:
  an elvish sword
  a small lantern (providing light)
  a backpack (being worn and open but empty)

>

events.intent: Look closely at the wall frescos for clues
events.response:
The frescos are faded from countless centuries.  It is diffifcult to make out 
the scene, but you can see that there are images of people around an arch.  
Given the faint colors and barely-recognizable costuming, you think one of the 
people in the image is none other than King Duncanthrax who created the G.U.E. 
centuries ago.  On this image, his eyes are still fresh-seeming; standing out 
from the rest of the faded image.

>
events.expected_outcome: Description of faded frescos, possibly hint at exit

events.intent: Inspect the unusual fresh eyes in the fresco image
events.response:
There is something about these eyes that seem to stand out from the rest of the 
image of the fresco.

>
events.expected_outcome: Closer detail on the fresh eyes in the fresco

events.intent: Press the striking fresco eye to find a hidden mechanism
events.response:
When you touch them, you get the feeling that they can be pressed inwards.

>
events.expected_outcome: Eyes respond or hint that both eyes matter

events.intent: Press the fresco eyes inward to open hidden mechanism
events.response:
You place your fingers onto the eyes of the fresco and push them inward.  They 
do, in fact, sink in slightly and you hear an audible click.  Around the edges 
of the fresco, dust falls as if pushed by wind behind the wall itself.  This 
fresco is most certainly a door that can be opened, you feel.

[Your score has just gone up by one point.]

>

events.intent: Open the fresco-door revealed by the eye mechanism
events.response:
You open the fresco.

>
events.expected_outcome: Fresco-door opens or hint to refer to fresco

events.intent: See the opened fresco passage
events.response:
Vault
This chamber is made of black stone.  The walls are pocked with age; showing 
faded frescos, the subject of which can no longer be determined.  The only exit 
is west, into a long. sloping tunnel that eventually leads back outside.  The 
weight of stone presses upon you, and you feel you must be deep underground.

>
events.expected_outcome: Vault with open fresco passage description

events.intent: Go through the opened fresco door
events.response:
Secret Passage
You are in a secret passage beyond the fresco wall.  The air is thick with dust 
that has not been disturbed in what must be a millenia.  There are dark 
passages to the north, east, and south.

>

events.intent: Press the striking fresco eye to find a hidden mechanism
Open the fresco-door revealed by the eye mechanism

>

events.intent: Explore the north passage
events.response:
Ancient Shrine
This is an ancient shrine.  A dust covered altar sits at the north wall.  On 
that wall is an engraving of a forgotten god.  Whatever treasures lay in 
offering have long since been pillaged.  On the floor are bones of a long-dead 
adventurer or pilgrim.

>
events.expected_outcome: New room description north of secret passage

events.intent: Inspect the dust-covered altar
events.response:
(the altar)
It is a simple affair since the engraving is complicated enough.  Whatever 
offerings were once left on this altar for this god have long since vanished.

>
events.expected_outcome: Details of altar, maybe item or mechanism

events.intent: Search the pilgrim bones for anything useful
events.response:
It seems to once have been a traveler or adventurer who met his fate down here 
long ago.

>
events.expected_outcome: Details of bones, possibly an item among them

events.intent: Pick up the old bones in case they are useful
events.response:
You'd rather not.

>

events.intent: Go back south to the secret passage
events.response:
Secret Passage
You are in a secret passage beyond the fresco wall.  The air is thick with dust 
that has not been disturbed in what must be a millenia.  There are dark 
passages to the north, east, and south.

>

events.intent: Explore the east passage
events.response:
Long Tunnel
You are in a long tunnel that runs east to west.  The walls are made of black 
stone and the passages stretch into ominous darkness.

>

events.intent: Continue east through long tunnel
events.response:
Intersection
This intersection is dominated by an ancient gate blocking passage to the east. 
Tunnels run north, west, and south; each into darkness.

>
events.expected_outcome: Further along tunnel or new room

events.intent: Try to pass east through the ancient gate
events.response:
(first opening the Ancient Gate)
It seems to be locked.

>

cases.failure_response:
When you touch them, you get the feeling that they can be pressed inwards.

>
cases.correction_response:
When you touch them, you get the feeling that they can be pressed inwards.

>
cases.review_notes: Independent exact endpoints and nearby/intervening raw SHA/text review. TOUCH EYE provides a clue but does not press the mechanism. Relabel as touching/examining or link subsequent PUSH EYES for the pressing intent.
cases.notes: Singular 'touch eye' accepted; response confirms eyes can be pressed inward, leading to push-eyes solution. No rejection to repair.

cases.intent: Open the fresco-door revealed by the eye mechanism
cases.review_notes: Independent exact endpoints and nearby/intervening raw SHA/text review. OPEN WALL explicitly opens the fresco after pushing the eye mechanism; positive control.
cases.notes: 'open wall' accepted as 'You open the fresco.' No rejection; shows parser maps wall to fresco-door.
